1	# Discord
2	
3	Connect a Discord bot to your Claude Code with an MCP server.
4	
5	When the bot receives a message, the MCP server forwards it to Claude and provides tools to reply, react, and edit messages.
6	
7	## Prerequisites
8	
9	- [Bun](https://bun.sh) — the MCP server runs on Bun. Install with `curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash`.
10	
11	## Quick Setup
12	> Default pairing flow for a single-user DM bot. See [ACCESS.md](./ACCESS.md) for groups and multi-user setups.
13	
14	**1. Create a Discord application and bot.**
15	
16	Go to the [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications) and click **New Application**. Give it a name.
17	
18	Navigate to **Bot** in the sidebar. Give your bot a username.
19	
20	Scroll down to **Privileged Gateway Intents** and enable **Message Content Intent** — without this the bot receives messages with empty content.
21	
22	**2. Generate a bot token.**
23	
24	Still on the **Bot** page, scroll up to **Token** and press **Reset Token**. Copy the token — it's only shown once. Hold onto it for step 5.
25	
26	**3. Invite the bot to a server.**
27	
28	Discord won't let you DM a bot unless you share a server with it.
29	
30	Navigate to **OAuth2** → **URL Generator**. Select the `bot` scope. Under **Bot Permissions**, enable:
31	
32	- View Channels
33	- Send Messages
34	- Send Messages in Threads
35	- Read Message History
36	- Attach Files
37	- Add Reactions
38	
39	Integration type: **Guild Install**. Copy the **Generated URL**, open it, and add the bot to any server you're in.
40	
41	> For DM-only use you technically need zero permissions — but enabling them now saves a trip back when you want guild channels later.
42	
43	**4. Install the plugin.**
44	
45	These are Claude Code commands — run `claude` to start a session first.
46	
47	Install the plugin:
48	```
49	/plugin install discord@claude-plugins-official
50	/reload-plugins
51	```
52	
53	**5. Give the server the token.**
54	
55	```
56	/discord:configure MTIz...
57	```
58	
59	Writes `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN=...` to `$DISCORD_STATE_DIR/.env` (defaults to `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/channels/discord`). You can also write that file by hand, or set the variable in your shell environment — shell takes precedence.
60	
61	> To run multiple bots on one machine (different tokens, separate allowlists), point `DISCORD_STATE_DIR` at a different directory per instance.
62	
63	**6. Relaunch with the channel flag.**
64	
65	The server won't connect without this — exit your session and start a new one:
66	
67	```sh
68	claude --channels plugin:discord@claude-plugins-official
69	```
70	
71	**7. Pair.**
72	
73	With Claude Code running from the previous step, DM your bot on Discord — it replies with a pairing code. If the bot doesn't respond, make sure your session is running with `--channels`. In your Claude Code session:
74	
75	```
76	/discord:access pair <code>
77	```
78	
79	Your next DM reaches the assistant.
80	
81	**8. Lock it down.**
82	
83	Pairing is for capturing IDs. Once you're in, switch to `allowlist` so strangers don't get pairing-code replies. Ask Claude to do it, or `/discord:access policy allowlist` directly.
84	
85	## Access control
86	
87	See **[ACCESS.md](./ACCESS.md)** for DM policies, guild channels, mention detection, delivery config, skill commands, and the `access.json` schema.
88	
89	Quick reference: IDs are Discord **snowflakes** (numeric — enable Developer Mode, right-click → Copy ID). Default policy is `pairing`. Guild channels are opt-in per channel ID.
90	
91	## Tools exposed to the assistant
92	
93	| Tool | Purpose |
94	| --- | --- |
95	| `reply` | Send to a channel. Takes `chat_id` + `text`, optionally `reply_to` (message ID) for native threading and `files` (absolute paths) for attachments — max 10 files, 25MB each. Auto-chunks; files attach to the first chunk. Returns the sent message ID(s). |
96	| `react` | Add an emoji reaction to any message by ID. Unicode emoji work directly; custom emoji need `<:name:id>` form. |
97	| `edit_message` | Edit a message the bot previously sent. Useful for "working…" → result progress updates. Only works on the bot's own messages. |
98	| `fetch_messages` | Pull recent history from a channel (oldest-first). Capped at 100 per call. Each line includes the message ID so the model can `reply_to` it; messages with attachments are marked `+Natt`. Discord's search API isn't exposed to bots, so this is the only lookback. |
99	| `download_attachment` | Download all attachments from a specific message by ID to `$DISCORD_STATE_DIR/inbox/`. Returns file paths + metadata. Use when `fetch_messages` shows a message has attachments. |
100	
101	Inbound messages trigger a typing indicator automatically — Discord shows
102	"botname is typing…" while the assistant works on a response.
103	
104	## Attachments
105	
106	Attachments are **not** auto-downloaded. The `<channel>` notification lists
107	each attachment's name, type, and size — the assistant calls
108	`download_attachment(chat_id, message_id)` when it actually wants the file.
109	Downloads land in `$DISCORD_STATE_DIR/inbox/`.
110	
111	Same path for attachments on historical messages found via `fetch_messages`
112	(messages with attachments are marked `+Natt`).
113
